thread:
Maria Chen: pushed a draft of new Grafana panels for GPU card degradation and wants feedback. link: https://grafana.redwood/team/gpu-degradation :eyes:
Samir Patel: taking a look now. what's the primary signal you want in the top-left panel? ECC counts or Xid rates?
Maria Chen: both. top-left = 5m rolling ECC corrected rate per-card, top-right = Xid31/Xid43 error spikes (rate per-hour), middle = regional unhealthy GPU ratio, bottom = time-to-drain after first Xid > threshold.
Lee Jackson: agree on Xid. practical note: Xid spikes are noisy from driver churn, we should debounce (5m -> 30m) for alerting.
Devon O'Neill: +1 on debounce. also we should differentiate persistent low-level ECC vs sudden spike. persistent low-level -> schedule replacement; spike -> drain if > 3 cards in 1 rack within 1h.
Anya Kuznetsova: propose a health score per-card: health = 1 - min(1, 0.6*norm_xid + 0.3*norm_ecc + 0.1*unready_flag) where norm_* are normalized to observed 99th pct. then region health = median(card_health) weighted by capacity.
Samir Patel: can you post a small formula snippet? easier for infra as code.
Anya Kuznetsova: sure: ```
# pseudo
norm_xid = min(1, xid_rate / xid_99)
norm_ecc = min(1, ecc_rate / ecc_99)
card_health = 1 - (0.6*norm_xid + 0.3*norm_ecc + 0.1*unready)
```
Maria Chen: nice. we'll show card_health heatmap and set two SLOs: regional availability >= 99.5% (P95 card_health >= 0.9) and mean-time-to-drain < 10m for spikes. Thoughts?
Lee Jackson: 99.5% seems ambitious in some APAC regions with older fleets. maybe tier SLOs: global-prod 99.7, regional-default 99.3, legacy 98.5.
Devon O'Neill: important: add a cost signal. draining aggressively on false positives spins up replacement GPUs and increases reserved capacity. We need a throttle: auto-drain only if card_health < 0.5 AND xid_rate sustained > 2x baseline for 30m. Otherwise create ticket for manual inspect.
Samir Patel: Also track correlation with kernel upgrades. CI deploys driver/kernel patches regularly. If we see Xid spike coincident with deploy time, suppress auto-drain for 60m. ci-bot: deploying kernel-driver v0.9.12 to us-west-2 at 1770345720 :deploy:
Maria Chen: good call. add a small panel that overlays deploy timeline on Xid graphs for quick triage.
ops-bot: alert: us-east-1 rack-7 gpu-23 Xid31 spike 1770345852 -> created incident INC-2127 :rotating_light:
Devon O'Neill: acknowledged, starting live triage. If next 10m shows decreasing Xid -> close. If persistent -> schedule replacement and mark node for drain.
Anya Kuznetsova: for dashboards, include per-card rolling quantiles (p50/p90/p99) not only rates. helps separate noisy single-card spikes from systemic degradation.
Samir Patel: one more: add a small cost delta panel: estimated monthly replacement + reserve cost if auto-replace enabled vs manual workflow. helps product decide right throttle.
Maria Chen: great feedback. I'll update the panels: add deploy overlay, health heatmap, p50/p90/p99 lines, cost delta. I'll also draft the SLO matrix with tiers and the auto-drain gating rules. Will drop the updated link in this thread shortly. :thumbsup:
Lee Jackson: thanks — will run through us-apac fleet and call out any region-specific thresholds.
Devon O'Neill: if anyone has historical Xid/ECC baseline spans (6-12 months) pls drop them here or attach in the dashboard datasource so normalizing works.
Samir Patel: uploaded `xid_ecc_baselines_2024-2025.csv` to the infra bucket. link: s3://redwood-infra/gpu/baselines/xid_ecc_baselines_2024-2025.csv
Maria Chen: perfect, grabbing it now. will push updates by EOD.
Anya Kuznetsova: small UX ask: when you click a card in the heatmap, show last 24h timeline + node metadata (model, bios, rack, purchase_date). speeds triage.
Maria Chen: noted. thanks all!
